messages:
alex: Quick heads-up: scheduling a schema change tonight 02:00 UTC. Were adding compressed_payload BYTEA (nullable) + streaming backfill job + a GIN index on the decompressed JSON for search. Staged rollout: canary (3 tenants) -> wave1 10% -> wave2 50% -> remainder. Any immediate objections?

jin: Migration summary: 1) ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN compressed_payload BYTEA; 2) backfill copies existing body->compressed_payload using pg_lz4 (non-blocking), job name payload_backfill_v1; 3) once backfill passes for a tenant we build index using function on decompressed json. Index creation will use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY with expression index on (jsonb_path_ops(decompress(compressed_payload))).

maria: Sounds invasive. What's the expected lock profile for the index build? Last time expression indexes showed unexpected bloat and locks.

jin: Index build should not take strong locks since CONCURRENTLY. But we saw spikes last time when many small transactions queued; watch for relation lock waits > 15s; replication lag > 2s is a red flag. Backfill is streaming with small batches by default.

alex: Ops ask: we should pin the service to v3.0.0 during wave1+2 to avoid reading partially-populated payloads in async workers. Will pin for 3 hours post-rollout. Also adding feature flag payload_search_enable.

deploybot: deploybot: scheduled migration 'mig-2026-06-payload-compress' -> canary on prod-staging 2026-06-12T01:00Z, prod wave1 2026-06-12T02:00Z. Abort instructions: react :x: within 8m of canary or `/deploybot abort mig-2026-06-payload-compress`.

sara: I'll draft release notes and add rollback steps. Also pinging infra to raise lock and replication alerts.

ops-bot: Temporary alert rule created: migration.payload.lock_watch -> triggers on any lock > 15s or any replica_lag > 2s. Pager duty route set to #oncall + sara.

maria: Proposal for abort conditions: 1) replica lag > 3s sustained for 3 checks, 2) any relation lock > 30s, 3) write p99 > 350ms or error rate spike > 0.75%. Abort action: disable payload_search_enable, stop backfill, pin older service version, open rollback incident.

jin: Agreed. Also fallback if expression index errors: build a partial index on top 10% hot tenants then schedule full offline index in low-traffic maintenance window.

alex: I'm on pager 01:50-03:30. I'll kick off canary and watch. @maria you own metrics. @sara owns release note + rollback doc.

deploybot: Canary started on prod-staging: simulated backfill on sample dataset. Smoke tests failed on one assertion (worker aborted when compressed payload decompression returned null for edge case).

jin: Investigating the assertion: edge-case nulls from third-party ingestion. I will patch worker to tolerate nulls and re-run canary. Rolling back the canary update for workers now.

alex: Good call. We'll pause the prod canary until worker patch is deployed. Reverting canary service shard.

sara: Updated release note to mention schema is safe but worker needs compatible runtime. Suggest we re-schedule prod canary for +30m after patch is live.

deploybot: Worker patch deployed to staging. Canary re-run scheduled 2026-06-12T01:40Z.

deploybot: Canary re-run success: backfill simulation passed; no lock alerts. Ready for prod wave1 at 02:00 UTC.

alex: Starting prod wave1 now. Remember throttle: concurrency=3, batch_size=2000, tenant_batch=10%.

deploybot: wave1 started. Monitoring channel #prod-payloads.

maria: Observed a short lock spike at 02:06 (15.8s) but alert threshold not breached. Replica lag peaked at 1.8s. Write p99 stable.

jin: Backfill job reported an expression-index partial failure on tenant T-42 at 02:11: runtime error when evaluating decompress() for a corrupted payload. Job paused for that tenant and moved on.

alex: Immediate actions: 1) disable payload_search_enable for T-42, 2) tag T-42 for manual investigation, 3) continue wave1. Is everyone ok with that?
maria: Yes. That matches abort matrix (we only abort for systemic issues). Isolated tenant corruption -> continue.
sara: Noting in release notes: tenant T-42 skipped index build due to corrupted payload. We'll run remediation script during maintenance.

deploybot: wave1 completed. Processed ~900k rows across canary+wave1. Two tenants skipped (T-42 and T-77). No global abort. Proceeding to wave2 in 20m if no anomalies.

ops-bot: Alert: detected relation lock 34s on events_payload_index_maintenance at 02:28. Triggering pause.

alex: Pausing wave2. Maria, confirm lock watch and metrics.
maria: Confirmed: one index worker got stuck waiting for autovacuum wrap; that's causing lock >30s. Error rate rose slightly but still under thresholds. Recommend reduce concurrency and run targeted autovacuum then resume.
jin: I'll reduce concurrency to 1 for index build and restart wave2 after autovacuum completes. Also enabling log level debug for backfill to surface corrupted rows.
sara: I'm updating the rollback doc to include the autovacuum mitigation steps.

deploybot: wave2 paused by operator at 02:33 UTC. Reschedule attempt in 10m.

ops-bot: Autovacuum triggered on affected table; expected completion ~5m.
deploybot: wave2 resumed at 02:45 UTC with concurrency=1 for index builds.

deploybot: wave2 finished at 03:10 UTC. Final tally: backfilled 4.8M rows, 5 tenants skipped for manual remediation, peak lock observed 34s (single event), replica lag peaked 2.4s during the stuck index (brief). We did not hit abort thresholds.
alex: Given the brief replication lag >2s, we kept within our abort thresholds but I'll extend the pin to 4 hours to be safe. We'll unpin after manual checks.
maria: I'll open a post-deploy check ticket and monitor overnight.
sara: Release notes published with instructions for rollback and remediation steps per skipped tenant.
jin: I'll prepare the remediation runbook and a script to repair corrupted compressed payloads (safe-guarded behind dry-run).

ops-bot: Cleanup: remove temporary alert at 06:00 UTC, archive job patch.

alex: Thread closed. If anything else crops up overnight please page me. Thanks everyone for quick triage on the index pause.
